doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: The East Village scene, Slugs and the hippies
summary: Ware moves to the East Village near Slugs, comments on the psychedelic scene and its decline, and plays club dates.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Anyway, we worked that little gig for about a month and I moved down -- I was staying up over in East Harlem. I moved down in the Village. That was during that period when the hippies (inaudible). The East Village was the "in" spot to be in.
Yeah. Slugs (PHONETIC) had opened up over there. They had quite a few little clubs, but it was all psychedelic things.
St. Lawrence was famous there, for psychedelic . . .

Yeah, but -- psychedelic. Joe Terminhi Pamhy (PHONETIC) and the Five Spot, they turned that corner into a little hamburger spot. That was it. No more nightclubs. So Electric Circus (inaudible). I don't got the name of that club. Tony Scott worked in there and a couple other little bands. But upstairs they had the main -- something like a disco. Oh, it was pretty famous. In fact, they shot a movie.
Right, yes, they did. I read about that.
Clint Eastwood was the star of it, whatever it was. Anyway, that whole neighborhood was pretty mean. Tompkins Square Park Thompson (unintelligible), they would congregate in there.
Yeah, on 10th Street. On 8th Street, really -- from 7th to 10th, on Avenue B and A. Anyway, I moved

down there on Avenue B, right around the corner from Slugs. So, I'd get a chance to see just about everybody, everybody that had a group come through, they'd work Slugs. So I'd hang out at Slugs and see what was going on. It was pretty nice for a while and then it got to be very raunchy.

Well, all during this period, '67 -- no, about the first part of '68, I started working little gigs with a pianist named Bill Trigilia from Jersey and we had jobs, Playboy Club and over in Jersey and it was kind of what you would call a club date, bar mitzvahs and Knights of Columbia, you know, good gigs.
